rationale:
bugs_open/283, round 3 — one narrow fix to the seam the council approved in round 2 (this correlation): DetectInstanceCollisions reports an IIFE-wrapped script as UNSCOPED whenever the body opens with a comment, because the accepted-wrapper regex anchors at the body's first byte.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW, MEASURED. Preparing the RFC_034 conversion programme, the detector was run over all 91 live getElementById component templates (cmd/instanceaudit, committed 9ef65953f, reads the live templates and calls the production function). It reported 88 of 91 as declaring into global scope. Sampling the flags found the real distribution: the estate's tool templates conventionally open their script with a /* tool-doc */ block, and 62 of the 88 are correctly IIFE-wrapped BEHIND that comment. With leading comments skipped, the corpus reads 66 scoped / 25 genuinely global — and the 25 are the 23 loanandmortgagecalculator calculators plus two tools, i.e. almost exactly the '22 templates' the original bug named.

A false flag here is not harmless conservatism, twice over. (1) The guard: once enforce_instance_scope is armed, a false UNSCOPED flag refuses renders of correct components. (2) The programme: RFC_034 uses this detector as the accept/reject gate for every conversion, and an unfixed gate would have routed 62 sound scripts into the judged-rewrite pool — the published '88 need script work' figure had already reached a filed RFC before sampling caught it, and has now been corrected in place there.

THE FIX IS DELIBERATELY MINIMAL: strip line and block comments from the FRONT of the body only, then apply the existing wrapper test unchanged. Comments elsewhere cannot sit between start-of-body and the wrapper, so nothing else changes; a leading comment in front of a genuinely global script still reports (asserted by a control in the test). The change makes the detector STRICTER-correct, not laxer: no script previously judged scoped can become unscoped, and the direction of error stays toward reporting (a wrapper shape the regex does not recognise still flags).

Inert in production in the same sense as rounds 1-2: nothing consumes {{.InstanceID}} yet (0 of 244 active templates, checked daily by the instance-token-adoption-check CronJob), and the guard that consumes this detector's verdict defaults to record-only.
submitter: 283 lane, round 3 (2026-08-17) — detector correction found while scoping RFC_034

plan.summary: DetectInstanceCollisions: skip LEADING comments before applying the accepted-wrapper (IIFE) test, so a /* tool-doc */ header does not make a correctly scoped script read as global. Measured on the live corpus: 62 of 91 templates were false-flagged; corrected distribution is 66 scoped / 25 genuinely global. One helper, one call-site change, one test with two controls, mutation-proven in both directions.

edits.rationale: reIIFE anchors at ^ so any leading comment defeats it. Skip leading comments only — a comment anywhere else cannot sit between start-of-body and the wrapper, so the narrow strip cannot launder anything.

The fixture is the real corpus shape (tool-css-unit-converter's opening), not one composed to make the point. Two controls: a leading comment in front of a genuinely GLOBAL script must still report (the strip must not launder), and an inner comment must change nothing (only leading ones are skipped).

grounded_in: Measured 2026-08-17, live corpus via cmd/instanceaudit (calls the production DetectInstanceCollisions): BEFORE the fix 3 scoped / 88 unscoped; AFTER 66 scoped / 25 unscoped. The 62-row delta is entirely templates whose body opens with a /* tool-doc */ comment followed by a verbatim IIFE — e.g. tool-css-unit-converter, whose body ends `})();`.

The 25 genuinely-global rows are: the 23 loans-*/mortgages-* calculators of loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk plus tool-archetype-clash-calculator and tool-bayesian-ranking — reconciling with the original bug's '22 calculator templates' scope.

All 20 inline on*= handlers and all 8 window.onload assignments in the corpus sit inside the genuinely-global set; zero window.<name>= assignments anywhere in the 66 — measured, which is what makes 'the wrapped ones are actually safe' a checked claim rather than an inference.

Mutation-proven both directions on a clean git-archive HEAD tree: removing the strip fails the leading-comment cases; making the strip return a constant IIFE fails the launder-control. Full suite green.

An independent hand-rolled Python classifier agreed 65/26 and was WRONG on the 26th (tool-css-specificity-calculator — regex literals in its JS unbalanced the crude depth walk; the template is a comment-led IIFE). The production detector, post-fix, is right on it. Recorded because it is this lane's recurring lesson: second implementations of an existing judgement disagree silently.

Adoption is still zero: 0 of 244 active templates reference {{.InstanceID}} (instance-token-adoption-check, daily 07:40 UTC, doc_notes subject_key='instance-token-adoption'), and enforce_instance_scope defaults off — so this change alters no production behaviour today.
plan.risks:
1. The strip is regex-based, like the detector it serves. A pathological leading construct (an unterminated block comment, a string that looks like a comment opener at byte 0) could confuse it — but the failure direction is unchanged: if stripping does nothing, the body reads unscoped, which is the pre-fix behaviour. The strip cannot make a global script read scoped unless the wrapper regex then matches a real wrapper, and the launder-control pins that.
2. This widens what the gate ACCEPTS, and the guard consuming it is the one that will someday refuse renders. The widening is exactly 'leading comments are invisible'; anything else that was flagged stays flagged. If a reviewer can name a script shape where a leading comment should legitimately change the verdict, that is the objection to raise.
3. The corpus figures above are a snapshot of 91 templates on 2026-08-17; the census is re-runnable (cmd/instanceaudit) and the RFC_034 programme should re-run it at execution time rather than trusting these numbers.
